title: Sawtooth (DCO)
what: The analog integrator saw, reset by the timer. Filter fully open. Pitch comes from a 48 MHz timer, so it is exactly in tune; the firmware scales the charging current with frequency to keep the amplitude constant.

title: Square / pulse wave
what: TIM2 CH2 output (0/5 V) mixed into the filter. 50 % duty = square: hollow, odd harmonics only.

title: Pulse-width sweep
what: The firmware moves the pulse width from 50 % to 5 % and back: the tone gets thinner and nasal.

title: PWM by LFO
what: A slow triangle LFO modulates the pulse width: the classic moving, chorus-like string/pad sound.

title: Sub oscillator
what: Saw alone, then the sub oscillator (square one octave lower, toggled in the timer interrupt) is switched on at 1.5 s: much more weight in the bass.

title: Noise through a resonant sweep
what: 16-bit LFSR noise (0/5 V from a GPIO) with the filter swept slowly at high resonance: wind.

title: All waveforms mixed: ladder drive
what: Saw, pulse and sub together push the transistor ladder into soft saturation (the input pair's tanh). Compare with the clean saw in example 1.

title: Cutoff sweep (24 dB/oct)
what: Saw at 65 Hz, cutoff swept from 40 Hz to 16 kHz and back, no resonance.

title: Resonance up to self-oscillation
what: Fixed cutoff (600 Hz); resonance raised from 0 to just past the self-oscillation threshold. The peak grows, the bass thins out (classic ladder 'bass loss'), then a sine starts to sing.

title: Resonant sweep
what: High resonance (0.9) and a cutoff sweep: the squelchy, vocal classic.

title: Self-oscillating filter as a sine oscillator
what: DCO silent, resonance above threshold: the filter itself is the oscillator. The firmware sets the cutoff per key; the pitch follows the expo converter (not temperature-compensated, so tuning is only approximate on real hardware).

title: Filter envelope amount
what: The same pluck with filter-envelope depth 0, 2, 4 and 6 octaves: from dull to 'wow'.

title: Keyboard tracking off / on
what: An upward scale with a fixed cutoff (high notes get dull), then with 100 % key tracking (the cutoff follows the note, constant brightness).

title: Amplitude envelope shapes
what: Pluck (fast decay), organ (gate), pad (slow attack and release): only the VCA envelope changes, generated in firmware and sent as CV_VCA.

title: VCA thump: untrimmed vs calibrated trim
what: Short bass notes. First half: VCA offset untrimmed (≈150 mV CV feedthrough, heard as a thump on every note). Second half: after the firmware trim calibration (< 1 mV).

title: Glide (portamento)
what: Firmware pitch slew between notes (timer periods updated every millisecond).

title: Vibrato (LFO → pitch)
what: Triangle LFO at 5.5 Hz, ±25 cent on the DCO timer — digital, exact and drift-free.

title: LFO → cutoff (wah)
what: LFO at 3 Hz sweeping the cutoff by ±2 octaves with resonance 0.7.

title: Arpeggiator
what: Firmware arpeggiator: hold a chord (Am7 → Fmaj7), the notes are played up/down in 16ths at 140 bpm.

title: Acid
what: Original 16-step acid bass line: high resonance, filter-envelope accents and slides.

title: Prelude
what: J. S. Bach, Prelude in C major BWV 846, bars 1–4 (public domain), as a 16th-note arpeggio with saw + pulse and a slow PWM.

title: Ode
what: L. v. Beethoven, 'Ode to Joy' (public domain) on a lead patch with sub oscillator, glide and vibrato.
